necessary_context.content: Choose x_t in P before loss f_t is revealed; incur f_t(x_t). For deterministic ONS, R_T=sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x_t)-min_{x in P}sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x). Horizon need not be known.
necessary_context.name: Online protocol and static regret

necessary_context.content: P is a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of R^n; D=max_{x,y in P}||x-y||_2. Losses are twice differentiable and convex unless stated otherwise; ||grad f_t(x)||_2<=G for every t,x. Alpha-exp-concavity means exp(-alpha f_t) is concave on P. Log denotes natural logarithm. ONS uses this class; no positive Hessian lower bound is imposed.
necessary_context.name: Standing assumptions and notation

necessary_context.applies_to: Proof of Theorem 2 up to its pre-simplification bound
necessary_context.content: Lemma 3 gives the gradient-based quadratic lower model for 0<beta<=0.5 min{1/(4GD),alpha}. Lemma 8 gives contraction toward any a in P under exact A-metric projection. Lemmas 11–12 give cumulative leverage <=log(det A_T/det A_0)<=n log(1+TG^2/epsilon), for A_t=epsilon I+sum_{i=1}^t g_i g_i^T and epsilon>0.
